newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ivory Coast 96/97 cocoa crop below 1 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast 96/97 cocoa crop below 1 mln tonnes.

text.p: Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa supplier, will produce a 1996/97 total cocoa crop of less than one million tonnes, agriculture and livestock minister Lambert Kouassi Konan said on Wednesday.
The figure is in line with recent government estimates but below private analysts' forecasts of up to 1.1 million tonnes.

"It will be less than one million tonnes," Kouassi told Reuters during a visit to Paris. " He said this represented a natural decline from the previous year's record harvest estimated at 1.2 million tonnes.
"You know that when a tree produces a great deal in one year, in the following year it takes a rest," he said, adding that such declines may also be affected by dry weather.
Rains favouring cocoa crop production ended in early February, although analysts have said that strong mid-crop (April-Sept) harvests are still expected.
The government's official forecast for the total crop, including the mid-crop, published in December is 950,000 tonnes.
Analysts have said that despite the dry weather, strong mid-crop harvests are still expected.
Weather up to April for mid-crop development will partly determine whether the government's forecast or the private estimates of more than one million tonnes turn out to be correct, analysts say.
An unexpectedly large 1995/96 mid-crop of 200,000 tonnes took Ivory Coast's total harvest to a record 1.2 million tonnes.
